name: Prednisone
executiveSummary: Intermediate-acting oral corticosteroid. Typical adult 5–60 mg/day by indication; pediatric anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive usually 0.5–2 mg/kg/day (high 2–3 mg/kg/day; maintenance ~0.25 mg/kg/day) with gradual taper.
indications:
## Indications

- Inflammatory, allergic, autoimmune, and hematologic diseases requiring systemic corticosteroids.
- Asthma/exacerbations (short courses), nephrotic syndrome, transplant rejection (specific regimens).
- Replacement / stress dosing in adrenal insufficiency (different physiologic doses).

## Precautions

- Uncontrolled active infections; caution in diabetes, hypertension, osteoporosis, psychosis, peptic ulcer.
- Prolonged therapy: HPA axis suppression risk — **do not stop abruptly**.
- In growing children prefer alternate-day/intermittent schemes when possible.

> Dose is highly indication-dependent; always follow the disease protocol.

adulto.dose: Anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive: usual **5–60 mg/day PO** in 1–4 doses (preferably morning). Short courses (e.g. asthma): often **40–60 mg/day** × 5–7 days. Chronic maintenance: lowest effective dose (often 5–10 mg/day). Stress/surgery: increase per adrenal insufficiency protocol.
adulto.administration: PO with food to reduce gastric intolerance. In prolonged regimens, concentrate morning dose or alternate-day per specialist.
adulto.notes: Approximate equivalence: 5 mg prednisone ≈ 4 mg methylprednisolone ≈ 0.75 mg dexamethasone.

pediatrico.presentation: Tablets; compounded oral solution by center.
pediatrico.dose: Label guidance (CIMA/Pediamécum): high **2–3 mg/kg/day**; intermediate **~1 mg/kg/day**; maintenance **~0.25 mg/kg/day**. Common anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive range: **0.05–2 mg/kg/day** in 1–4 doses. Asthma/exacerbation: **1–2 mg/kg/day** × 5–7 days (adult max **60 mg/day**), with taper if the course is prolonged.
pediatrico.administration: PO; tablets may be split per order. Prefer morning dosing in prolonged therapy.
pediatrico.notes: Titrate by disease (nephrology, rheumatology, hematology have their own schemes). Monitor growth, glycemia, and BP in prolonged use.

neonatal.dose: No single regimen; neonatal corticosteroids (e.g. BPD) use specific schemes (often dexamethasone/hydrocortisone). Prednisone only under neonatology.
neonatal.notes: Risk to neurodevelopment and adrenal axis; not an antipyretic/analgesic.

stability:
## Stability / storage

- Tablets: room temperature, protected from moisture per label.
- Compounded solutions: follow institutional pharmacy beyond-use date.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Insomnia, increased appetite, fluid retention, hypertension, hyperglycemia, gastritis, mood changes. Prolonged: iatrogenic Cushing, osteoporosis, myopathy, cataracts, immunosuppression, growth delay, adrenal insufficiency on withdrawal.
